[b]An-Nabai News[/b]

[u]ANM and HIA Banned; Government Says They Were Behind Coup Attempt, Terror Plots[/u]

[i]23 April 2026 CE  6 Dhul Qidah 1447 AH[/i]

Medinah al-Islam Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi issued a rare Executive Decree today after fajr, immediately banning the Helpers of the Righteous (ANM is the Arabic abbreviation) and the Arab Socialist Party (HIA) parties, expelling their representatives from the Grand Majlisi, freezing their accounts, and putting their leaders under criminal investigation. Sultan al-Ayyubi gave a speech after issuing the decree, in which he accused these parties of conspiring to overthrow him in a coup attempt last year and seeking to carry out major terrorist attacks against the government and minority ethnic and religious communities. Supporters of the government say there is sufficient evidence after thorough investigations of the coup attempt and foiled terror plots by all the major intelligence agencies.

However, supporters of the banned parties and some independent observers of the political situation say this appears to indicate a major power grab by the governing coalition.

Listen, I am fully aware of the supposed putschists arrested last year for the coup attempt against al-Ayyubi, as everyone in this country is. They are members of the HIA who also were known to collaborate with the ANM on the basis of the enemy of my enemy is my friend, not very upright citizens, stated Mahmoud al-Barartiyeh, president of the College of Social Sciences and professor of political science at the University of Medinah al-Islam. But in terms of political arrests and charges, data collected from the National Security Organizations database shows that over the last 4 years, these parties members make up 85% of ALL political arrests and 95% of all political convictions. Absolutely incredible, considering these parties typically never poll above 10% nationally, combined, and that they only have 55 delegates in the entire Grand Majlisi. In shaa Allah, the truth of this matter will be brought to light. 

I think most people know these parties are basically just the legal outlet for two major groups of extremists was the response from Ahmed ibn Said Qarandi, Baladullahan national and international election observer and head of the NGO Election Watch. After the dictatorship [the military Arabist-Salafi dictatorship of Abdullah al-Qurshi from 1956 to 1978], these forces had been completely banned from all forms of political participation. 

But after major protests and deliberations, they were allowed to politically participate as a result of the constitution of 1992. Despite that, and the fact that many of the lower level members of the dictatorships security forces were pardoned after the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of 1979-1981, it is a hard fact that Arabists have carried out 7,650 acts of racist violence that have led to over 3,500 deaths since 1982, while Salafi terrorists have carried out 9,500 or more attacks and killed or injured 12,500 people since 1982, mostly between 1982 and 1992, but a third of these attacks were after 1992. Its hard for me to believe that there is literally NO overlap between such extremists and the HIA and ANM.
Other headlines:
[u]New Grand Majlisi Elections to be Held in 3 Months; HIA and ANM to Appeal their Bans; Protests Against the Bans and in Support of them Across Baladullah; Rioting in Maghlara, 500 People Arrested, 45 Injured Including 15 Police[/u]
[/spoiler]

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;60391170][b]The Regency August-November, 2026[/b]
The dissolution of the Empire of Elesyr-Vespurias had left a major scar upon the face of politics in Thýven, highlighting ultimately the deep divisions which had begun to appear upon the political scene and among the parliament. 

Following the formal abdication of Emperor Erjk Drs, and the seemingly reluctant acceptance of Crown Prince Filljp to take the throne, the Gøsfodde would take matters into their own hands, moving to make the Steward of the Royal House, Bjørn Nalin, the de facto head of state for Thýven, ushering in what many called, The Regency. 

The appointment of Bjørn Nalin was already contested by members of the Gøsfodde who had felt that Bjørn had failed to curtail the powers of Erjk Drs during the Elesyro-Vespurian ascendancy, thereby becoming complicit to the overreach of the prior monarch. As a result the various Fondenfoddels would reorganise themselves into pro and anti-regency camps. Though the matter was much more complex, as even the anti-regentists merely wanted a different regent in the stead of Bjørn. 

As a result of the division in the Gøsfoddde, the Council of Princes would step into action, moving quickly to formally dismiss Nalin as Chief Steward, in the absence of a head of the council. However, this would serve to enrage the regentists who would take to the streets to protest the actions of the Unelected Council. 

Fearing for the stability of the nation, the Princes would call upon the armed forces to take charge in restoring order, with the National Reserves being summoned out from their places to serve the crown. However, due to the dissolution of Elesyr-Vespurias, and the lack of proper transitional plans being made on Thývens side, the armed forces and reservists were without allegiance to any one state, thus causing a breakdown in the central command as generals and ranking officers refused to act against the protestors. 

The Gøsfodde, fearing for their own safety, and for the complete breakdown of constitutional order would call upon the firmest ally of the state, the Christian Orthodox Church of Thýven, calling upon Patriarch Cyril Mendenav to act as a mediator between the peoples and the princes. However, the Patriarch would refuse to mediate on a matter of state politics in order to avoid crossing wires with the church and the state.

Protests would continue in the streets as the Council of Princes, upon hearing the rejection of the patriarch to mediate, began to pressure the patriarchate to move from its neutral stance, citing the lack of military cohesion, and the separation of the Gøsfodde. After three weeks of back and forth between the patriarchate and the council, Mendenav would agree to mediate, summoning all involved parties into a special plenary session of the state.

[b]The November Council, November 2026[/b]
The Plenary Council, or November Council as it would become colloquially known among the media, would consist of representatives from the various parties of the state, including Filljp Drs as a member of the Council of Princes, representing the crown, Piter Drømm, Steward of the Royal House Pro-Tempore who was appointed by a vote of the Gøsfodde to act as a representative of the legislature, General Albin Erjisson for the armed forces, and Patriarch Mendenav as chief mediator. 

Four main points would be agreed upon by the November Council: 
[list]1. The Armed Forces were loyal to the head of state and legislature
2. A new constitution would be needed and a constitutional convention formed.
3. The crown would be temporarily suspended from formal government functions until the new constitution was written, and elections were held. Wherein the powers of the executive would rest in the Gøsfodde
4. The Council of Princes would be disbanded until a new government was formed.[/list]

Following this, the results of the council would be read aloud in the public square overlooking the Palace of the Legislature to a crowd of 134,000 protestors, who would widely acclaim  the council's decision, though a clear amount of disgruntlement remained due to a desire for a more open and equal government. 

Thus with the masses subdued, the government would move quickly to gather various political thinkers and legislators would be brought forward to begin the process of drafting a new constitution for the nation.

[b]The 2026 Constitutional Convention 1st Session: November-December 2026[/b]

Following the November Council's final meeting and promulgation of the Articles of Unity on November 10, 2026, the Gøsfodde would immediately move to form the Council for Constitutional Matters, summoning forth members of the legislature from all the Fondenfoddel and various constitutional scholars from across the nation. 

[i]Opening Session: November 15, 2026[/i]
The Opening ses
sion would be overseen by Patriarch Mendenav, who would bless the proceedings before laying out the procedural rules which had been voted on November 11-12th by the Council for Constitutional Matters. The initial debates would revolve primarily around the powers of the executive, which in the 1865-66 constitution had been broadly defined as having near total control over the powers of the executive. However, this broad and vague assumption of powers had led to the Elesyro-Vespurian abuses, which saw the illegal assumption of Imperial titles without the consent of the legislature, or the Council of Princes. As a result it would be generally agreed that the powers of the executive, if the monarchy should remain the chief guiding force of the country, were to be limited or lessened to the original mindset of the authors of the 1865 constitution, as participating in the government, but not able to override the government nor will of the people. However, as to what the exact powers of this limited monarchy should be were heavily debated. Following a procedural vote to end the day, the first session was closed with some progress being made. 

[i]2nd Session: November 16, 2026[/i]

The second session would be overseen by Patriarch Mendenav once again, who had been formally made head of the convention by a vote towards the end of the day (110 for, 10 against). The second session continued moving to address the executive controversy, with a small division arising over whether the head executive should have control over military affairs, or whether they should merely oversee the affairs with the Steward of the Royal House acting as chief of the armed forces. Those against moving the power of military from the executive stated that the executive gave a strong image to the armed forces, and a solid long-lasting individual which the leadership could rely on, to centralise the forces. Those who supported it, argued that the abuses of the dictatorship of the 30s-70s by the military were enough evidence to show that a centralised head could be abused. During the session, a bloc, known as the Council of the Peoples consisting of Piter Drømm, and thirteen other representatives, who had been liaisons to the citizens and press for the session, came forward with a proposal to allow for both a centralised command and head, while also placing secure bounds by the legislature on the full powers over the armed forces, namely war, which would be required to be approved by the legislature, this move would be widely agreed upon, with little issue, though contentions still remained over the separation of executive and legislature with this proposal. 

 Following a procedural vote to end the day, the second session was closed with some progress being made, with agreements being made to continue in two days. 

[i]3rd Session: November 18, 2026[/i]

The third session would be overseen by Patriarch Mendenav once again, who would move to address the question of exactly who the acting head of state was, requesting that a formal decision be made by the end of the week, and a formal appointment be made.

However, arguments arose following the request from Mendenav over whether he had overstepped his own authority, and whether the election should be public and free or directly chosen by the legislature. While there were those who wished to bend to the whims of the people, like Piter Drømm, others argued that getting the votes of millions of citizens in merely a week would take time, not to mention the coalescing of candidates for the position. Once again, the question of who held the power would arise once more as tensions began to rise in the council chambers. The 3rd session would come to an abrupt end following a fist fight breaking out after a major disagreement on the powers of the new executive were contested, with representative Jormen, a military veteran claiming that the military was the only stable form of executive, thus suggesting to a greying of the line of the military and civil government, an offensive suggestion to most who knew or remembered the abuses of the military junta of the 50s-60s. 

[i]4th Session: November 19, 2026[/i]

Discussion would reopen in the fourth session on who should lead the country, and how it would be done, as a result of the sidetracking of the third session, the council would be split into two sub-councils, one for the election of the new executive, and another for the constitution, with the two meeting at the end of the day to unify their discussions. The fourth session would reach consensus about not permitting military or formal noble members to head the state

[i]5th Session: November 20, 2026[/i]

The opening of the fifth session would note the creation of the Thýven Transitional State wherein the state would formally be headed by an executive officer and the constitutional council until the new government could accede to its full power upon the deadline set during the 4th session which was to be March 1st 2027.

The council would address concerns regarding a potential electoral system involving the formation of a special council of electors, composed of the nobility and the members of the Orthodox Church. The primary issues being that to have such a body would undermine the ideals of democracy. In order to quell majority dissent, the patriarch would propose a bicameral structure, replacing the former unicameral structure that had persisted under the 1865 constitution. It would be agreed that a special plebiscite  on the matter would be held on November 25th in order to ensure an open democratic process.

[b]A Republican Crusade | Erene200 | Second Flouesch Republic[/b]

Friedrich Müller watched the countdown on the screen before him, flanked by the flags of the Second Flouesch Republic on both sides. He looked into the sea of reporters before him, from all over the continent of Vespurias, abroad or even local news stations in Floueschia. Behind him was Emily Schiltz. Grinning at what was about to be announced, Gonthier Fuelenger, preparing to make his own statement on the matter, meanwhile across the hull Klos Reuter was running from office to office in the foreign ministry, trying to get every diplomat on standby for the wave of calls from other countries that would surely follow. He knew that an invasion this early into the Republic's existence would be seen as an aggressive strike at best, slightly panking.  Muller knew he only had one shot at this, the National People's Army were already in position across the border. For months now, after the beginning of Operation Mockingbird, they had been slowly building up a force of 52,350 Men, 130 Main Battle Tanks, 95 Howitzers, and 1,663 thousand other pieces of equipment. Accompanying them were over 240 aircraft stationed and ready to go in airbases near the border, their pilots anxiously sitting in their hangars, waiting for the alarm to sound. Across the border, towns were already being evacuated by the Internal Revolutionary Guard out of precaution. Muller looked around the room one last time, closed his eyes and held his breath before reading out his speech.

"Fellow citizens of our dear and blessed Republic. Friends of Freedom, Democracy, and Liberty across the world!

Our Great Republic has prospered thus far. Like its former royalist co nation, Nevonia was a land split into, first, its developed north, and then its extremely mountainous South. A fact that the Ieweschte Revolutionär Kommando, or the IRK, was uniquely aware of. Since the creation of the IRK, confrontation or even an invasion of its former co-national partner in Nevonia had always been one of its chief preparedness priorities. This was because large remnants of royalist armies crossed the border and continued fighting the NVA from Nevonia, long after the general capitulation of royalist forces. The biggest issue with their planning would be the timeframe of the invasion, while Nevonia was at this point in a state percipatory to a complete civil war with open fighting in the streets. The National People's army was in no state for a long, drawn-out conflict with Nevonia. Firstly, while the National People's Army had a lot more equipment in its possession than most, most obtained due to royalist paranoia. It did not have enough for the complete mobilization of its forces, in fact by the time that the National People's Army was completely ready to go and mobilized on the Nevonian border an inventory of the NVA revealed that it had completely ran out of tanks, meaning that the nation would have to turn to its mothball stockpile of older tanks from the 70s and 60s if they planned to replace their losses.

Secondly, the NVA had never actually fought a conflict as an organized force; much of the revolution was characterized by violent irregular warfare across cities and rural areas. Not the new Combined Arms Warfare doctrine that the IRK had based much of its plans around. Compounding this was that many veterans, tired from nearly 6 years of war, had taken the option to discharge themselves during the transitional period, where much of the Revolutionary Army was broken up into the IRG and NVA. While victory in the revolution had inspired hundreds of thousands of youth to volunteer themselves in the NVA and IRG. This led to a loop where an experienced officer would retire, and an inexperienced recruit would be forced to take their place due to a lack of other options. The IRK had initially proposed to the first consul that rehabilitating royalist officers would not necessarily be a bad idea. This request was rejected on hand out of fears that the Radical Republicans would leave the governing coalition if this were done. However, the National People's Army had one major advantage over the Nevonian Army, and that was its air force. The air force during the war had almost completely defected to the Republican Forces, meaning that it didn't suffer the same brain drain in experience that other branches of the NVA did. 

After analyzing the state of the National People's Army, the Ieweschte Revolutionär Kommando developed 4 key objectives for the invasion of Nevonia that were presented:

1. Overthrow the Royalist Regime within 4 months of the National People's Army entering the country

2. Utilize superiority in Air Equipment to quickly eliminate Nevonia's air force and secure air superiority

3. Leave a reasonable reserve of manpower to cover the southern flank

4. Within 2 months build a capable revolutionary republican army to assist in sweeping up any remaining royalist forces.

With these objectives in mind, the IRK would authorize the deployment of 5 divisions to the border of Nevonia. These being the 1st Panzer Division under the command of Lieutenant General Paul Weber, the 1st Panzergrenadier Division under the command of Lieutenant General Marie Hansen, and the 1st Infantry Division under the command of Lieutenant General Claire Klein. Marc Hoffmann would take up the position as Field Marshall of the 1st Army which all of these divisions would belong to. Additionally, 2 divisions of the Internal Revolutionary Guard, 1 organized to act as a rapid support force and the other as an occupational force, would be moved to the border under the command of Second Lieutenant Sophie Wagner. 

On the morning of Saturday, April 15th. The NVA, IRG, and IRK received direct orders from the Council of State to begin the invasion, the invasion began with a coordinated hurricane bombardment; all of the howitzers within each division suddenly and without warning began to fire in the direction of close, nearby, and known targets that the state had given them weeks prior. Over 10,000 shells were fired in a single hour as the border was peppered with artillery. While this bombardment was ongoing, the Loftwaff, who had received advanced warning of the strike order, had taken off from the air base at Flooxhoven. This base was one of the largest in the country and hosted 150 aircraft. These aircraft were split into 2 groups, 100 Vaab 37s, which had orders to begin striking bridges, power substations, nevonian storage facilities, and forward positions. Their secondary objective was to provide close air support to ground units. These were older aircraft and therefore far more expendable to the IRK than others. Meanwhile, the remaining 50 Jaas 39s were to go for longer strike missions; they would hit large airbases, power substations near the capital, government buildings and offices, major infrastructure targets such as roads that could be used to reinforce the border. 5 Jaas 39s were sent with the specific mission of destroying the Nevonian Royal Palace by dropping 500 kg bombs on it. Another key objective was bombing Nevonian Facilities.

Once the hour-long hurricane bombardment had concluded, ground forces would not move in for another hour; this was mostly to allow howitzer units enough time to resupply to be able to provide regional artillery support. Given that after the bombardment would have at least dazed the nevonian royal army it can be assumed that the forces to cross the border, that being armored forces would be able to slice through whatever remained of the Nevonian Border Defences like butter, in a particular case the border city of Ketan, largely considered a sister city of Aardbur would be quickly overrun by the 2nd Armored Battalion, the royalist commander in charge of the city's defense had been killed in the initial strikes and his second in command ordered the city abandoned, upon the NVA entering the city they would be greeted by cheering crowds, offering flowers, bread and other gifts to the NVA. Nevonian republican forces would join up with the NVA in the city as the 2nd Armored Battalion continued their advance down the coast. The last units to cross into the border would be the occupational division of the IRG, who would set up their command center in Ketan's City hall before dispatching occupational forces to various captured towns along the borders.

Meanwhile, at home, the IRK ordered the immediate preparation of 50 Main Battle Tanks, 100 Howitzers, and almost 10,000 small arms from the National Mothball. This meant that equipment from facilities across the nation was to be sent by rail to factories to be refitted or refurbished before being sent out to the frontline. The IRK also began looking into ordering more equipment from either abroad or from domestic manufacturers. Additionally, the mobilization of the IRG's 3rd Division for occupational duties was ordered; all of this activity would likely take another month.
